Antinuclear antibodies (ANA), double-stranded DNA antibody levels to screen for systemic lupus erythematosus
The humoral immune system abnormalities observed in silicosis include an increased incidence and titer of rheumatoid factor, antinuclear antibodies, and immune complexes.
Rheumatoid factor, antinuclear antibodies, and non-organ specific antibodies may be present in the blood.
Antinuclear antibodies screening due to association with autoimmune diseases such as SLE.
anti-smooth muscle antibodies, antinuclear antibodies; type-2: anti-liver/kidney microsomal type 1
Antibodies to smooth muscle, antinuclear antibodies, and low thyroid hormone levels may also be present.

qs.q: Why are antinuclear antibodies (ANA) screened in patients being evaluated for inflammatory myopathies?
o: Because of their link to autoimmune diseases like SLE
qs.e: Antinuclear antibodies screening is performed due to the association of inflammatory myopathies with autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus. They do not screen for viral hepatitis or gastrointestinal malignancies.
